title: Kambala
summary: After the rice harvest, the farming villages of coastal Karnataka flood a long mud track and race pairs of buffaloes down it. A runner stands on a plough-board behind each pair, steering through the splash while calling to them to go faster.
howToPlay: Hold the pad to let the pair run; let go to ease them while their strength comes back.
When the ring closes on the pad, press once on the stride to add a splash-sprint.
Run through the splash lines in good time, keep your calls steady, and reach the end of the track before the other pair.
Three short heats; your score is the average of the three.
rules: The track is short, about 140 metres, so every heat is a quick burst.
Holding spends the pair's strength; letting go to trot refills it.
A press that lands on the stride gives a burst; one off the stride only unsettles the pair.
The soft flooded mud shrinks the timing window for everyone.
Each splash line is cleared cleanly only if your stride is steady as you reach it.
The animals are called and urged, never struck.
heritageNote: Kambala is a farming-season race of the flooded paddy tracks of the Tulu country in coastal Karnataka, held in the cool months after harvest. Villagers keep their pairs for the sport and families gather along the track; care for the animals comes first.
